- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast peak at 10–15% above recent high.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope downward after day 10–15.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early in the period; apply downward correction of 1–3% for first 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “1.00” (strong bullish) followed by “0.00” (neutral), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 2–4% after day 10.
